title: Blepharoplasty,  Eyelid Surgery, and Brow Lift

criteria.criterion: For the purposes of this policy, these surgeries (either individually or in the minimum combination required to achieve a satisfactory surgical outcome) are functional when overhanging skin or upper lid position secondary to dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis, or pseudoptosis is sufficiently low to produce a visually-significant field restriction considered by this policy to be approximately 30 degrees or less from fixation.
criteria.source_quote: For the purposes of this policy, these surgeries (either individually or in the minimum combination required to achieve a satisfactory surgical outcome) are functional when overhanging skin or upper lid position secondary to dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis, or pseudoptosis is sufficiently low to produce a visually-significant field restriction considered by this policy to be approximately 30 degrees or less from fixation.
criteria.reviewer_note: background definition; the checkable parts are BLE-C05 to BLE-C08

criteria.criterion: Published literature correlates this amount of field restriction with a Margin Reflex Distance (see below) of 2.0 mm or less.
criteria.source_quote: Published literature correlates this amount of field restriction with a Margin Reflex Distance (see below) of 2.0 mm or less.
criteria.reviewer_note: background on why 2.0 mm is used; covered by BLE-C06/C07

criteria.criterion: When a noncovered cosmetic surgical procedure is performed in the same operative session as a covered surgical procedure, benefits will be provided for the covered procedure only.
criteria.source_quote: When a noncovered cosmetic surgical procedure is performed in the same operative session as a covered surgical procedure, benefits will be provided for the covered procedure only.
criteria.reviewer_note: billing rule, not a clinical criterion

criteria.criterion: Reasonably complete information fulfilling the criteria in Section A (Patient Complaints and Physical Signs), and Section B (Photographs) as delineated below must be adequately documented in the patient’s medical records to demonstrate the reasonableness and necessity of the procedure(s) performed.
criteria.source_quote: Reasonably complete information fulfilling the criteria in Section A (Patient Complaints and Physical Signs), and Section B (Photographs) as delineated below must be adequately documented in the patient’s medical records to demonstrate the reasonableness and necessity of the procedure(s) performed.

criteria.criterion: A functional deficit or disturbance secondary to eyelid and/or brow abnormalities must be documented, such as interference with vision or visual field that impacts an activity of daily living (such as difficulty reading or driving).
criteria.source_quote: A functional deficit or disturbance secondary to eyelid and/or brow abnormalities must be documented, such as interference with vision or visual field that impacts an activity of daily living (such as difficulty reading or driving).
criteria.question: Does the note document a functional problem caused by the eyelids or brows, such as blocked vision or visual field affecting daily activities (for example reading or driving)?

criteria.criterion: Ptosis with a margin reflex distance (MRD1) of 2.0 mm or less
criteria.source_quote: A margin reflex distance (MRD sometimes referred to as MRD1)) of 2.0 mm or less.
criteria.original_criterion: For Blepharoptosis Repair - A margin reflex distance (MRD sometimes referred to as MRD1)) of 2.0 mm or less.
criteria.question: Does the note document ptosis with a margin reflex distance (MRD1) of 2.0 mm or less?

criteria.criterion: Redundant upper lid skin hanging over the lid margin with a pseudo-MRD of 2.0 mm or less
criteria.source_quote: Redundant eyelid tissue hanging over the eyelid margin resulting in pseudoptosis where the “pseudo” margin produces a central “pseudo-MRD” of 2.0 mm or less, or
criteria.original_criterion: For Upper Blepharoplasty and/or Brow Ptosis Repair - Redundant eyelid tissue hanging over the eyelid margin resulting in pseudoptosis where the “pseudo” margin produces a central “pseudo-MRD” of 2.0 mm or less, or
criteria.question: Does the note document excess upper eyelid skin hanging over the lid margin (pseudoptosis) to within 2.0 mm of the pupil center?

criteria.criterion: Redundant lid tissue medially or laterally that obscures the line of sight
criteria.source_quote: Redundant eyelid tissue predominantly medially or laterally that clearly obscures the line of sight in corresponding gaze.
criteria.original_criterion: For Upper Blepharoplasty and/or Brow Ptosis Repair - Redundant eyelid tissue predominantly medially or laterally that clearly obscures the line of sight in corresponding gaze.
criteria.question: Does the note document excess eyelid tissue that blocks the line of sight?

criteria.criterion: When requested documentation does not meet the criteria for the service rendered or the documentation does not establish the medical necessity for the services, (i.e., illegible or incomplete) such services will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
criteria.source_quote: When requested documentation does not meet the criteria for the service rendered or the documentation does not establish the medical necessity for the services, (i.e., illegible or incomplete) such services will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.

criteria.criterion: Photographs documenting the eyelid findings are referenced in the record
criteria.source_quote: The “physical signs” documented in Section A must be clearly represented in photographs of the structures of interest and the photographs must be of good quality and of sufficient size and detail as to make those structures easily recognizable.
criteria.original_criterion: The “physical signs” documented in Section A must be clearly represented in photographs of the structures of interest and the photographs must be of good quality and of sufficient size and detail as to make those structures easily recognizable.
criteria.question: Does the note mention photographs documenting the eyelid findings?

criteria.criterion: Unless medial/lateral gaze is required to demonstrate a specific deficit, photos should be with gaze in the primary position, looking straight ahead.
criteria.source_quote: Unless medial/lateral gaze is required to demonstrate a specific deficit, photos should be with gaze in the primary position, looking straight ahead.
criteria.reviewer_note: photo technical detail; not checkable from an operative note

criteria.criterion: Oblique photos are only necessary if needed to better demonstrate a finding not clearly shown by other requested photos.
criteria.source_quote: Oblique photos are only necessary if needed to better demonstrate a finding not clearly shown by other requested photos.
criteria.reviewer_note: photo technical detail; not checkable from an operative note

criteria.criterion: Digital or film photographs are acceptable, and may be submitted electronically where possible.
criteria.source_quote: Digital or film photographs are acceptable, and may be submitted electronically where possible.
criteria.reviewer_note: photo technical detail; not checkable from an operative note

criteria.criterion: Photographs must be identified with the beneficiary’s name and the date.
criteria.source_quote: Photographs must be identified with the beneficiary’s name and the date.
criteria.reviewer_note: photo technical detail; not checkable from an operative note

criteria.criterion: If the eyelid obstructs the pupil, there is a clear-cut indication for surgery.
criteria.source_quote: If the eyelid obstructs the pupil, there is a clear-cut indication for surgery.
criteria.question: Does the note document that the eyelid covers or obstructs the pupil?

criteria.criterion: For reference, the colored part of the eye is about 11 mm in diameter, so the distance between the light reflex and the lid would need to be about one fifth that distance or less for the MRD to be 2.0 mm or less.
criteria.source_quote: For reference, the colored part of the eye is about 11 mm in diameter, so the distance between the light reflex and the lid would need to be about one fifth that distance or less for the MRD to be 2.0 mm or less.

criteria.criterion: Two photos are needed:One showing both eyes of the patient at rest demonstrating the above MRD criterion in the more ptotic eye, and another showing both eyes of the patient with the more ptotic eyelid raised to a height restoring a normal visual field, resulting in increased ptosis (meeting the above MRD standard) in the less ptotic eye.
criteria.source_quote: Two photos are needed:One showing both eyes of the patient at rest demonstrating the above MRD criterion in the more ptotic eye, and another showing both eyes of the patient with the more ptotic eyelid raised to a height restoring a normal visual field, resulting in increased ptosis (meeting the above MRD standard) in the less ptotic eye.
criteria.reviewer_note: photo technical detail; not checkable from an operative note

criteria.criterion: If both a blepharoplasty and a ptosis repair are planned, both must be individually documented.
criteria.source_quote: If both a blepharoplasty and a ptosis repair are planned, both must be individually documented.
criteria.reviewer_note: applies only when both procedures are planned

decision_rule.explanation: A documented functional deficit and photographs are required, plus at least one physical sign (MRD of 2.0 mm or less, pseudoptosis, tissue obscuring the line of sight, or lid obstructing the pupil).

question_note: Each kept criterion is asked as a yes/no question about the note. 'met_if' says which answer satisfies the criterion; 'if_not_mentioned' is used when the note is silent (silence is fine for prohibitions such as sedation, but not for required findings).
